note.p: John Flather was Patrick Patrickson's closest college companion and family friend of the Godwins since 1808 (see Locke). In her Journal, Mary Shelley described Flather as the 'true assassin' of Patrickson' and in the same volume an editorial note identifies Flather as a sizar at St John's College Cambridge.

The identification is not certain, particularly as Patrickson and Flather appear to have no relationship in the diary (althogh this makes sense given Mary Shelley's comments). However, Flather calls on Godwin on the 9 Aug 1814, the day after Patrickson dines with Godwin and the day before he kills himself, suggesting some relationship.

Ed Pope adds: Flather senior was probably the father, Thomas Flather who was buried at St Botolph Aldersgate 28.5.1815 age 67 from Duke-st. His will PCC 8.8.1815 dated 18.12.1814 tin plate worker mentioned his daughter Elizabeth his wife Elizabeth his three sons Thomas, James and John, and his friend John Bentley esq of Highbury-house. He married Elizabeth dau of John Bull of Needham Market, Suffolk at St Bartholomew the less 28.6.1778. Their children were Thomas born 24.2.1780, James born 10.6.1783, John born 31.3.1786 and Elizabeth born 22.8.1787. all at 35 Little Britain and all registered at Dr Williams' Library. John was the only son to go to university and became a barrister dying in 1875. Thomas and James stayed in the metal trades Add new comment
